parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes to work with local authorities to give first-time buyers priority on new homes and introduces a permanent mortgage guarantee scheme. On renters, Labour commits to ensuring private rented sector homes meet minimum energy efficiency standards by 2030.

citations.quote: Labour will work with local authorities to give first-time buyers the first chance to buy homes and end the farce of entire developments being sold off to international investors before houses are even built.
We will ensure homes in the private rented sector meet minimum energy efficiency standards by 2030, saving renters hundreds of pounds per year.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives propose passing a Renters Reform Bill to deliver fairness for both landlords and renters, including abolishing Section 21 no-fault evictions once court reforms are in place, while also strengthening grounds for evicting tenants guilty of anti-social behaviour.

citations.quote: We will pass a Renters Reform Bill that will deliver fairness in the rental market for landlords and renters alike.
We will deliver the court reforms necessary to fully abolish Section 21 and strengthen other grounds for landlords to evict private tenants guilty of anti-social behaviour.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords, alongside proactively enforcing clear standards for socially rented homes.

citations.quote: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords.
Proactively enforcing clear standards for homes that are socially rented, including strict time limits for repairs.
